config.mpegtsHint: Service identifiers and transport-stream parameters. Required for strict middleware (Otrum) and hospitality TVs (LG Pro:Centric etc.). Defaults are fine for a single channel — if you run multiple channels on the same multicast subnet, assign distinct Service IDs.
config.serviceNameHint: Shown in the channel list on the receiver (SDT service_name).
config.serviceProviderHint: Broadcaster name (SDT service_provider). Examples: "LiveQX", hotel name.
config.serviceIdHint: program_number in PAT. Range 1..65535. Channels sharing a multicast subnet MUST have distinct Service IDs, otherwise middleware collapses them into one program.
config.transportStreamIdHint: TSID of the transport stream (SDT/PAT). Range 1..65535.
config.originalNetworkIdHint: ONID of the source network (SDT). Usually 1 for private networks; a registered value for public ones.
config.muxRateHint: Constant mux rate: 0 = VBR (default), >0 = enables null-packet stuffing to the given rate. Set to video bitrate + audio bitrate + ~15 % headroom for strict middleware.
config.sdtPeriodHint: SDT repeat period. 0 = FFmpeg default (500 ms). Some middleware wants ≤ 2000 ms.
config.patPeriodHint: PAT/PMT repeat period. 0 = FFmpeg default (100 ms). Strict middleware expects 40–100 ms.
config.videoCodecHint: H.264 is the default for modern receivers. MPEG-2 is only for legacy hospitality set-tops that don't decode H.264 reliably. MPEG-2 is always CPU-encoded — any GPU mode is ignored when this is selected.
config.presetNotApplicableMpeg2: MPEG-2 has no x264-style preset; only bitrate applies.
config.audioCodecHint: AAC-LC is the default for modern receivers and OTT. MP2 (MPEG-1 Layer II) is the classic DVB audio codec for hospitality set-tops that lack AAC licensing or read the PMT stream_type strictly.
config.maxBHintH264: 0 disables B-frames (lowest latency). 2–3 is a good default for OTT/live. Higher values improve compression at the cost of decode delay.
config.maxBHintMpeg2: DVB and set-top boxes traditionally expect the IBBP cadence (2 B-frames). Values above 2 are technically valid but may confuse legacy hardware decoders. 0 disables B-frames entirely.
config.gopSizeHintH264: Distance between key-frames. 0 = auto (equal to FPS, ≈ 1 s). Larger values improve compression; smaller values reduce channel-switch delay. HLS/OTT often uses 2×FPS for finer seek granularity.
config.gopSizeHintMpeg2: Distance between key-frames. 0 = auto (max(FPS/2, 6), i.e. ~0.5 s — the DVB set-top expectation). Broadcast IPTV typically uses 12–15 frames at 25 fps.
config.h264ProfileHint: H.264 profile constraint. Middleware/set-top boxes may require a specific profile: cheap hospitality decoders often lock to Main@3.1; modern boxes handle High. Wrong profile = decode failure. Baseline forces CABAC off (poor compression).
config.h264LevelHint: H.264 level caps bitrate, buffer size and frame dimensions the decoder must support. Match to your resolution/FPS: 3.1 for SD, 4.0 for 1080p 30, 4.2 for 1080p 60, 5.1 for 4K 30. Wrong level = non-compliant stream some decoders refuse.
config.mpeg2ProfileHint: MPEG-2 profile constraint. Consumer DVB/IPTV set-tops universally decode Main (MP) — that is the SD broadcast norm. Simple (SP) drops B-frames for cheap decoders. High (HP) adds SNR scalability rarely used in practice. 4:2:2 is a studio contribution profile — do not use for delivery.
config.mpeg2LevelHint: MPEG-2 level caps resolution and bitrate. Counter-intuitively, LOWER ordinal means HIGHER capability (spec quirk): Low=10 (352×288), Main=8 (720×576/480, ≤15 Mbps — SD DVB), High-1440=6 (1440×1152, ≤60 Mbps), High=4 (1920×1152, ≤80 Mbps). MP@ML (main/8) is the safe default for SD DVB-C/S/T set-tops.
config.bitrateModeVbr: variable with peak ceiling (unicast, HLS, RTMP)
config.bitrateModeHint: CBR is mandatory for MPEG-TS multicast — the fixed VBV envelope is what set-top boxes and hospitality decoders rely on. VBR gives better quality-per-byte on unicast delivery (HLS/RTMP) but breaks MPEG-TS PCR timing. CRF is a quality target for OTT/archive; on GPU and MPEG-2 backends it silently downgrades to VBR (backend logs a warning).
config.bitrateMaxHint: Ceiling for VBR mode in kbps. 0 = auto (encoder picks 1.5×bitrate — enough headroom for scene changes without doubling the pipe width). Ignored outside VBR.
config.crfHint: Constant Rate Factor: lower = better quality, larger file. Sensible range 18..28; 23 is libx264 default. 0 = default. Only meaningful on x264 — GPU and MPEG-2 backends fall back to VBR.
config.preloadSecHint: How many seconds to prefetch from the source. Applied on next channel start.
config.timezoneHint: IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Moscow). Used to interpret schedule windows. Applied on next channel start.
config.modeNoneHint: Channel doesn't read files from disk. Plays only the live source — e.g. a transcoded SRT relay.
config.modePassthroughHint: Files are read straight from the given directory. New files appear instantly, but a share outage takes the channel offline.
config.modeCacheHint: Background daemon syncs share → local cache; the channel plays from cache. Resilient to network drops, but consumes disk space.
config.sinkNoneHint: Nothing is recorded. You can't reconstruct what played and when.
config.sinkFileHint: Daily JSONL files under the channel's playback/ directory. Read with grep/tail; rotation is manual.
config.sinkDbHint: Shared SQLite for all channels. Fast search and reports; entries older than N days are auto-purged.
config.stoppedRequired: Channel must be stopped to edit this section.
config.rawHint: Submit a JSON patch (RFC 7396). Server rejects immutable fields (resolution, fps, id, name) and refuses outputs[] mutations — use /outputs endpoints.

masterKey.title: Master Key
masterKey.warnFileInStateTitle: The key sits next to the data
masterKey.warnFileInState: Any copy of the state directory (backup, VM snapshot, disk image) carries the key together with the data it protects, so the encryption no longer helps. Keep the key outside the state directory and back it up separately from the data.
masterKey.rotationHint: Rotation is CLI-only with the engine stopped. No REST endpoint by design.
masterKey.rotationHintFile: The key is a file. Stop the service and run these commands (the data key changes, secrets are re-encrypted, the old key stays next to it as a .bak file):
masterKey.rotationHintPassphrase: The key is protected by a passphrase. Stop the service and run these commands: you will be asked for the passphrase, and the new data key keeps the same one.
masterKey.rotationHintCredential: The key is a systemd credential. Stop the service and run these commands: the new key is encrypted with systemd-creds and the old credential stays next to it as a .bak file.
masterKey.rotationHintEnv: The key is passed in the LIVEQX_MASTER_KEY environment variable. It cannot be rotated here: set a new value yourself and re-encrypt the secrets. See the knowledge base article "Master key".
masterKey.rotationHintEnvFile: The key is passed as a separate file (usually a systemd credential). It cannot be rotated here: create a new credential and re-encrypt the secrets. See the knowledge base article "Master key".

tls.title: TLS
tls.httpInsecure: Plain HTTP — control-plane is not encrypted
tls.modeAutoDesc: Internal CA + server cert managed by the engine. Clients must trust the CA below.
tls.modeProvidedDesc: Operator-supplied cert/key. Use Import to update; the engine never overwrites your PKI on its own.
tls.modeBehindProxyDesc: TLS terminates upstream (nginx / Caddy / Traefik). Core listens plain HTTP only inside the trusted perimeter.
tls.modeDisabledDesc: TLS disabled. Allowed on loopback or with allow_insecure_bind=true. Do not use in production.
tls.caHint: Distribute this PEM to users so their browsers trust the engine. Each download is recorded in the audit log (tls.ca_export).
tls.subject: Subject
tls.regenerateHint: Re-issues server.crt under the existing CA. Listener restarts immediately; the CA stays unchanged so existing user trust survives.
tls.regenerateUnavailable: Available only in `auto` mode. Current mode: {{mode}}.
tls.regenerateConfirm: This will re-issue the server certificate and immediately restart the TLS listener. Continue?
tls.importDescription: Upload an operator-supplied cert + private key (and optional CA). The engine validates the keypair and chain before promoting; old files stay untouched on failure.
tls.importHint: PEM files only. The private key gets chmod 0600 after promotion. Listener restarts on success.
tls.serverKeyHint: Matching private key. Stored with mode 0600.
tls.importCaHint: If provided, the engine verifies the chain cert→ca and refuses on mismatch.

gateways.title: Gateways
gateways.createSubtitle: Configure a new ingest gateway. The gateway starts in stopped state.
gateways.name: Name

gateways.rebindHint: Address/port/interface changes require stop → patch → start (socket rebind).

fec.label: FEC (forward error correction)
fec.editorHint: Toggling enabled or saving any field hot-swaps the gateway (brief stop → re-create → start).
fec.hotSwapWarn: Save will briefly stop the gateway and restart with the new FEC config. Output ports may change if column/row offsets are edited.

modePlain.passthrough: Takes an incoming stream and forwards it to one or several addresses as-is. Doesn't inspect payload, adds minimal latency. Use it when you just need to fan out a signal.
modePlain.demux: The incoming stream carries several TV channels bundled together (typical for satellite or DVB). The gateway splits them into individual channels and sends each to its own address.
modePlain.remux: The opposite of Demux: takes several separate channels and combines them into one bundled stream. This is how cable operators broadcast.
modePlain.transcode: Re-encodes video and audio with new parameters (bitrate, resolution, codec). The most resource-intensive mode — noticeably loads CPU or GPU.

form.demuxPlain: Each route says which channel (by service_id from the incoming multiplex) goes to which of your outputs. Add one route per channel you want to keep.
form.remuxPlain: The output is a single combined multiplex assembled from every input. The IDs below are service identifiers for PSI tables; usually the defaults are fine.
form.transcodePlain: Bitrate is in bits per second (4,000,000 = 4 Mbps). Resolution, FPS, GPU and encoder presets are configured on the gateway page after creation.
form.fecPlain: Recovers lost packets on the receiver side. Useful on unstable links. Adds roughly 10–25% to bandwidth usage.
form.demuxHint: Each route maps an input service_id to an output ID. Add at least one route.
form.demuxEmpty: No routes — add at least one to demultiplex.
form.targetBitrateHint: 0 = no NULL stuffing. Set ≥ Σ(inputs) for CBR.
form.transcodeHint: Codec settings (resolution, fps, GPU, presets) live in the Detail page after creation.
form.fecPassthroughWarn: FEC for passthrough is not supported yet — use Demux mode with a single * route as workaround.
form.addressInputHint: 0.0.0.0 binds all NICs; multicast group requires a valid join address.
form.ifaceHint: Pick a NIC by name to bind explicitly. Leave empty for kernel default.
form.autostartHint: If enabled, the gateway starts automatically on core boot.

pairing.title: Pairing package: {{name}}
pairing.once: The token in the package is shown once. After this window is closed it cannot be seen again. If the package is lost while the screen is not enrolled, issue a new token.
pairing.howTo: Hand the file to the screen's computer and enrol the player with it.
pairing.copyFailed: The browser would not copy. Select the text above and copy it by hand, or download the file.

actions.moveRule: A move is possible inside your object and only between groups where you have the move right.
actions.noTargets: There is no group you may move this screen to. You need the "move screens" mark on another group of the same object.
actions.tokenText: Earlier tokens stop working. The new token is shown once with the pairing package. This is possible while the screen is not enrolled.
actions.reenrollText: The old device stops working at once: its certificates are revoked and its open connection to the broker is cut. The screen goes back to "Awaiting enrolment" and you get a package with a new token for the new device.
actions.reenrollTextRevoked: The screen becomes "Awaiting enrolment" again and you get a package with a new token. The earlier certificates stay revoked.
actions.reenrollKeeps: The name, the group and the whole history stay; the identifier is the same.
actions.revokeText: The screen's certificates stop working: it can no longer reach the server or get commands, while its record and journal stay. To connect a device again use "Bind again".
actions.reasonHint: Goes to the log. Up to 200 bytes.
actions.reasonBad: The reason is too long or has control characters.
actions.deleteText: The screen is deleted with its command history and event journal, and its certificates are revoked. This cannot be undone.

errors.forbidden: No right for this move. Inside an object you need the move right on both groups; between objects an administrator moves.
errors.not_found: Screen not found. It may have been deleted already.
errors.group_not_found: That group no longer exists. Refresh the page.
errors.already_pending: The screen is not enrolled yet: it needs a new token, not a re-binding.
errors.not_pending: A token can only be issued to a screen that is not enrolled yet.
errors.not_configured: The screens module is not set up: the addresses are missing.
errors.ca_unavailable: The server has no root certificate for screens.
errors.invalid_reason: The reason is too long or has control characters.
errors.storage_error: The server could not do it. Try again later.

commandResults.expired: the screen got it too late
commandResults.unsupported: the screen does not know this command
commandResults.failed: the screen could not do it
commandResults.os_not_rebooted: the screen answered but the computer did not reboot
commandResults.no_confirmation: the screen did not confirm in time
commandResults.broker_error: the broker did not accept the command
commandResults.broker_not_connected: the server is not connected to the broker

list.title: Screens
list.treeFailed: Could not load the list of places.
list.loadFailed: Could not load the list of screens.

empty.title: No screens yet
empty.text: The screens you have access to appear here. If you expect a screen and it is missing, ask an administrator for rights on its object or group.

noMatch.title: Nothing found
noMatch.text: Change the search or the status.

detail.notFound: Screen not found. It may have been deleted, or you may have no rights on its place.
detail.pendingNote: The screen is not enrolled yet: it has not used its enrolment package. There is no data about it until then.
detail.revokedNote: The screen was revoked {{when}}: its certificates no longer work and no commands are sent to it.
detail.staleNote: The screen is offline: below is what it last reported.

commands.title: Commands
commands.none: No commands have been sent to this screen.

objects.title: Objects and groups
objects.lead: An object is a place where screens stand, such as a shop floor or a warehouse. Inside an object, screens are collected into groups. Rights and commands are given by these places.
objects.noGroups: This object has no groups yet. A screen cannot be enrolled without a group.
objects.deleteObjectBlocked: Object "{{name}}" cannot be deleted while it has groups. Delete the groups first.
objects.deleteGroupBlocked: Group "{{name}}" cannot be deleted while it has screens. Move the screens to another group first.
objects.loadFailed: Could not load objects and groups.

empty.title: No objects yet
empty.text: Create the first object, then add a group to it — after that screens can be enrolled.

confirm.deleteObject: Object "{{name}}" will be deleted. Users' rights on it go too.
confirm.deleteGroup: Group "{{name}}" in object "{{object}}" will be deleted. Users' rights on it go too.

nameErrors.tooLong: The name is too long: at most 120 bytes
nameErrors.badChars: The name must not contain control characters

serverErrors.name_taken: This name is already used at this level
serverErrors.invalid_name: The name is not acceptable: empty, too long or with control characters
serverErrors.not_empty: Cannot delete: there is still something inside. Refresh the page and check
serverErrors.not_found: Not found: it may have been deleted already. Refresh the page
serverErrors.storage_error: The server could not save the change. Try again later

settings.title: Screens: settings
settings.lead: These addresses and limits apply to the whole screens module. The addresses go into the pairing package of every new screen.

notConfigured.title: The addresses are not set yet
notConfigured.text: Until the three addresses in the first block are filled in, a new screen cannot be paired: the server will answer that the module is not configured.

serverErrors.invalid_server_url: The server did not accept the address: use https://host[:port] with no path
serverErrors.invalid_device_api_url: The server did not accept the address: use https://host[:port] with no path
serverErrors.invalid_mqtt_broker_url: The server did not accept the address: use mqtts://host[:port]
serverErrors.invalid_ca_cert_pem: This does not look like a PEM certificate

addresses.title: Addresses for screens
addresses.hint: A screen takes them from its pairing package and then connects by them on its own. After pairing they need changing only if the server's address changes.

server_url.label: Server address (pairing and administration)
server_url.hint: Like https://host or https://host:port, no path. https only.

device_api_url.label: Device port address (status and certificate renewal)
device_api_url.hint: A separate port where the server checks the screen's certificate. For example https://host:8444.

mqtt_broker_url.label: Command broker address (MQTT)
mqtt_broker_url.hint: Screens receive commands through it. Like mqtts://host:port, for example mqtts://host:8883.

token_ttl_days.label: Pairing token lifetime, days
token_ttl_days.hint: The token is given once, with the pairing package. After this time it can no longer pair a screen, but a new one can be issued.

clock_policy.label: Clock check on new screens
clock_policy.hint: Applied by default to the screens you create.
clock_policy.relaxed: Relaxed: for networks without accurate time
clock_policy.relaxedWarning: The relaxed check does not compare the validity dates of the server's and broker's certificates: a screen will accept even an expired certificate from our authority. The risk is low in a closed local network; do not enable it for a server reachable from the internet.

ca_cert_pem.label: Root certificate (PEM)
ca_cert_pem.hint: Leave empty to use the certificate that signed the server's own certificate. Fill in only if screens must trust a different root.

commands.title: Commands to screens
commands.hint: How long a command lives and how long the server waits for an answer. Times are in seconds, with a familiar form beside them.

command_ttl_s.label: Command lifetime, s
command_ttl_s.hint: If a screen does not receive the command within this time (switched off, no network) it is dropped and will not run later.

confirm_timeout_restart_s.label: Wait for a player restart to be confirmed, s
confirm_timeout_restart_s.hint: If the screen does not confirm in this time the command counts as unanswered and the screen can be restarted again.

confirm_timeout_reboot_s.label: Wait for a screen reboot to be confirmed, s
confirm_timeout_reboot_s.hint: Rebooting the computer takes longer, so the time is longer.

confirm_timeout_reload_s.label: Wait for a playlist reload to be confirmed, s
confirm_timeout_reload_s.hint: A screen confirms this command at its next “I'm here” signal.

command_batch_size.label: Batch size for a command to many screens
command_batch_size.hint: A command to a group, an object or everyone goes in batches: the next one when the previous is confirmed.

command_batch_stop_percent.label: Stop if more than this share did not come back, %
command_batch_stop_percent.hint: If more than this share of a batch fails to confirm, the remaining batches are not sent.

retention.title: Keeping the logs
retention.hint: Closed records older than the limit are deleted once a day. Deletion cannot be undone. Unconfirmed commands and jobs in progress are never deleted.

events_retention_days.label: Screen events, days
events_retention_days.hint: Coming online and going offline, version changes, commands.

commands_retention_days.label: Closed commands and jobs, days
commands_retention_days.hint: The outcome of a command (confirmed or not answered). The fact of sending is kept separately in the audit trail.

broker.title: Command broker (MQTT)
broker.lead: The server sends commands to screens through the broker and learns that a screen has switched on. Without the broker, screens are still visible by their regular “I'm here” signal, but commands do not reach them.
broker.loadFailed: Could not get the broker status.

disabled.label: Off
disabled.text: The link to the broker is switched off in the server configuration (players.broker.enabled). Commands to screens and instant appearance online do not work; screens are seen only by their regular signal.

waiting.label: Waiting
waiting.text: The server cannot connect until everything needed is in place — see the list below.

connecting.label: Connecting
connecting.text: The server is trying to connect to the broker. Commands are not going out yet.

connected.label: Connected
connected.text: All is well: commands go out, and screens show as online as soon as they switch on.

stopped.label: Stopped
stopped.text: The link stopped together with the server.

readiness.title: Is everything ready
readiness.hint: The server connects to the broker once everything in the list is in place.

mosquitto_in_build.label: This server build supports MQTT
mosquitto_in_build.fix: This build was made without the MQTT library. A build with support (libmosquitto) is needed.

device_ca.label: The device authority exists
device_ca.fix: The device authority is created once when the server is prepared (the root is kept separately). Until then the server cannot get an identity for the broker.

trust_root.label: There is a root certificate to check the broker with
trust_root.fix: A root certificate that signed the broker's certificate is needed: either the server's own, or yours in Settings (the “Pairing” block).

broker_url_configured.label: The broker address for screens is set
broker_url_configured.fix: Fill in “Command broker address” in the module settings.

reconcile.title: Reconciling with the broker
reconcile.hint: The server brings the screens' records on the broker in line with its database: when a screen is created or revoked, after each connection, and by itself every {{interval}} s. So a screen created while the broker was down is not lost.

crl.title: Revocation list
crl.hint: If a screen is stolen or retired, its certificate is revoked. The broker keeps such a screen out when it is given this list.
crl.off: The list is not passed to the broker (the mode is off in the server configuration). A revoked screen loses all rights on the broker and is disconnected, but may connect again and do nothing. For full protection set players.broker.crl.mode = local.
crl.reloadFailed: The list is written, but the broker could not be told

reloadErrors.pid_file_unreadable: the broker's process-id file cannot be read
reloadErrors.bad_pid: the process-id file holds a bad value
reloadErrors.process_not_running: the broker process is not running
reloadErrors.not_the_broker: the process at that number is not the broker
reloadErrors.signal_failed: the signal to the broker could not be sent

crl.soon: The list is close to its end. The server renews it daily; if that is not happening, the broker will stop admitting anyone. Check the errors above.

connection.title: Server connection to the broker
connection.hint: Change it only if the broker moved. A new address is first tried with a test connection and saved only if the broker answers.
connection.disabledHint: The link is switched off in the server configuration, so here you can only see how it is set up.

host.label: Broker address
host.hint: A name or IP address the server can see. Often 127.0.0.1 when the broker is on the same machine.

interval.label: How often to reconcile with the broker, s
interval.hint: From 10 to 86400. Reconciliation also runs at once when a screen is created or revoked.

verify.label: Check the broker's name in its certificate
verify.hint: Protects against a fake broker. Leave it on.
verify.warning: The check is off: the server will not notice a broker being replaced, by name. Turn it back on as soon as the broker has a certificate with the right name.

errors.host: Letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore and colon are allowed

serverErrors.invalid_host: The server did not accept the address
serverErrors.invalid_port: The server did not accept the port
serverErrors.invalid_reconcile_interval_s: The server did not accept the interval
serverErrors.broker_disabled: The link to the broker is switched off in the server configuration

connection.checkOk: The broker answered; connecting is possible. Nothing was changed.

probeFailed.title: The broker did not answer at the new address
probeFailed.text: Nothing was changed; the old address stays in force. Reason:
probeFailed.skip: Save anyway, without testing (the broker is not up yet). The server will start connecting at the new address.

connection.applied: Connection changed; the server is reconnecting
connection.mayTakeAWhile: The test can take up to 8 seconds

warnings.verify_hostname_disabled: Checking the broker's name is off. Turn it on when you can.
